business_scope.primary_industry_name: Search Engine Optimization Data Crawler and Keyword Analytics Tool

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state autonomous commercial register for LLC formation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Civil Law codified system built on the Napoleonic/French model; Islamic Sharia is the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Constitution of 2014. Commercial and company matters are governed by codified statutes, not common law precedent.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 27 June 1992)
Egypt–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (1976, most-favored-nation clause)
Egypt–European Union Association Agreement with investment provisions (in force 2004)
Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (1980)
Treaty Establishing the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA, 1994)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (joint stock, partnership and limited liability companies), as extensively amended by Law No. 148 of 2017, reading the UBO/beneficial-owner disclosure obligations administered by GAFI; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, art. 66, and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017); Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014; Executive Regulations of the AML Law as issued and amended by the Prime Minister, together with the binding AML/CFT regulatory decisions of the Central Bank of Egypt and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each non-resident corporate shareholder evidencing legal existence and the UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State, commercial register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — notarization in the country of origin, certification by the competent ministry or authority, then legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate; Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or equivalent shareholders' resolution of each foreign corporate shareholder authorizing formation of the Egyptian LLC, appointment of its manager, and allocation of share quotas
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Statutory corporate body of the foreign shareholder with notarial attestation in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — notary, competent central authority, then Egyptian Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed by each non-resident shareholder or UBO appointing the founding manager and/or incorporation counsel with express powers to sign the memorandum, open bank accounts, and complete GAFI, tax and commercial registry filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — notary, competent central authority, then Egyptian Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and source-of-funds declaration of all UBOs, directors, managers and authorized signatories, including a legalized corporate organigram where a corporate shareholder sits above the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin for the certification of identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — notary certification followed by Egyptian Embassy/Consulate legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and credit standing letter from the principal bank of each non-resident corporate shareholder, confirming account conduct, source of funds and ability to remit the LLC's capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The overseas banking institution, with notarial attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — notary attestation followed by Egyptian Embassy/Consulate legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-sign-off screening of the entity and of all UBOs, shareholders, directors, managers and POA holders against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List (1267/1986/1988 and successor regimes), (ii) the OFAC SDN List and applicable OFAC sanctions programs affecting Egypt, (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and (iv) the EMLCU domestic watchlists published in the Egyptian Official Gazette. Screening must run through vendor-based real-time sanctions databases and be manually cross-checked, with archived results retained for at least five years. Any hit requires enhanced due diligence covering source of funds, source of wealth and a written compliance opinion before any GAFI submission. PEP status of the individual, including family members and close associates under FATF methodology, requires enhanced due diligence under Law No. 80 of 2002; for this low-risk MarTech/SaaS ISIC 6201 entity, standard onboarding applies upon a clean screen. The payment rails selected (Stripe and Paddle) independently perform KYB/KYC and sanctions screening and may block settlement where UBO profiles fail their automated checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — 'Invest in Egypt / Al-Mostatmar' one-stop-shop electronic portal (https://www.investinegypt.gov.eg); the cleared name is subsequently entered in the commercial registry's 'Tajree' system operated by the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The LLC must have a mandatory Arabic statutory name appearing in the bilingual memorandum of association; a Latin-only name is not acceptable for the corporate form. A phonetic English/Arabic transliteration may be registered as the secondary trading style for cross-border SaaS branding, and the Arabic name must not duplicate, conflict with, or be misleadingly similar to an existing registered Arabic name or a well-known foreign trademark. The proprietary SEO product brand may be protected separately as a trademark, but the Arabic corporate name governs all GAFI, commercial registry and tax certificates.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Finance (unless the entity is licensed as a financial institution)
Islamic or Sharia (requires prior Al-Azhar or competent ministry approval)
Suez Canal (requires Suez Canal Authority consent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: if the initial 30-day reservation lapses, the applicant re-submits the name clearance request through the GAFI portal with payment of the applicable tariff. Rejection appeal: within 15 days of the rejection notice, the applicant files a written administrative grievance with GAFI's investment grievance committee, annexing a trademark register search certificate, evidence of distinctiveness, a list of similar existing names and counsel's representations that the proposed name is not misleading and does not violate public order. If the administrative reconsideration is denied, the decision may be challenged before the State Council (Administrative Court) within 60 days of notification. Parallel re-filing of a clean alternative name is the standard expedient; no statutory stay of incorporation attaches to the pending appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not fully permissible. Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976 and Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 require every LLC to maintain a physical head office address in Egypt, which must appear in the commercial register, tax card, e-invoicing profile and statutory books. A licensed serviced-office or flexible-business-center lease, with physical reception, meeting facilities and a lease contract, satisfies the commercial substance requirement for this ISIC 6201 SaaS/analytics risk tier. A mailbox-only or PO Box-only virtual office is non-compliant and would expose the entity to GAFI and tax authority queries.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated below 10% annualized probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a low-risk, license-exempt, purely digital software and analytics entity under GAFI's risk-based administrative matrix. Desk-based substance verification, including annual financial statements, e-invoice continuity, VAT filings and a substance questionnaire, is routine; a non-responsive registered office or mismatched lease documentation materially raises the likelihood of an inspection and adverse compliance findings.

GAFI LLC incorporation filing and registration fee (e-formation dossier, MOA review, standard two-shareholder track)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per page for certified translations including notarial attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Serviced-office registered address letter of intent and first-quarter reservation deposit for the commercial substance requirement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a physical serviced suite with reception, mail handling and lease documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per UBO and sanctions screening package for a single low-risk LLC

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company secretary and corporate legal counsel fees for pre-incorporation due diligence, MOA drafting, name clearance handling and supervision of the full filing process
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian law firm / GAFI-licensed incorporation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for a standard LLC incorporation and stage-one due diligence engagement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2020), Articles 1–20 (Incorporation), Article 28 (Paid-up Capital), and Executive Regulations of the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) Law No. 72 of 2017
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Registration Department, Cairo Headquarters
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (notarized by a licensed Egyptian notary public)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum under Companies Law 159/1981 as amended; however, a capital adequacy of at least USD 1,000 equivalent in EGP is recommended to secure bank verification and GAFI pre-registration approval. Required initial capital must be deposited in a temporary treasury escrow account at an Egyptian commercial bank; release follows issuance of the commercial registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the members hereby adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association and subscribe to the fully issued share capital of EG_LLC. RESOLVED that the registered office shall be located at the registered address in Cairo, Egypt. RESOLVED that the principal business purpose shall be development and operation of Search Engine Optimization Data Crawler and Keyword Analytics Tool (ISIC 6201). RESOLVED that Directors shall be authorized to open bank accounts, appoint legal counsel, and execute all constitutional and regulatory filings. RESOLVED that the Chairman, General Manager, and Company Secretary are appointed as first corporate officers with authority to sign and represent the company within legal limits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name approval and Legal Form Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) – Name Reservation Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online via GAFI OSS portal for name availability check for the proposed LLC suffix, select the preferred trading name (must not conflict with reserved or registered trademarks), upload a name reservation form signed by founding shareholder(s). Upon approval, the name is reserved for 60 days. Pay EGP 250 name reservation fee via the portal.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport or national ID copies of all founding shareholders
Certificate of non-conflict issued by national trademark office (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or offensive content, submit a revised name to the same GAFI desk. If rejection is based on trademark opposition, file an opposition settlement or choose an alternate distinctive name and rerun the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authentication and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Department of the Ministry of Justice and GAFI Attestation Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic (or bilingual with Arabic controlling) and have each shareholder sign in the presence of an Egyptian notary public. Following notarization, submit the attested copy to GAFI attestation unit to validate the signatures and verify compliance with standard form requirements.
required_dossiers: Certified true copies of shareholder identity documents
Original signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Draft company bylaws with details on management structure and share classes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises deficiencies in document grammar or legal clauses, revise the document with the assistance of a licensed corporate lawyer and re-notarize. If GAFI queries corporate purpose definitions, clarify the purpose language to explicitly cover software development and SaaS delivery.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Certified commercial bank under Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the LLC's name at a GAFI-approved commercial bank (e.g., Bank of Alexandria, NBE, or similar branch). Deposit the subscribed capital (in EGP equivalent of USD) with proper source-of-funds documentation. Bank issues a capital deposit certificate (certificate of blocked funds availability) to be attached to the GAFI application.
required_dossiers: Bankky brand name confirmation letter issued by GAFI
Initial draft Memorandum of Association
Board or shareholders' minutes authorizing the capital deposit
Proof of identity and address of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence on source of funds, provide sworn declaration of liquidity, audited financial statements of shareholders, and employment or corporate references. If verification delays persist, escalate to the GAFI banking facilitation unit to enforce service-level resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) – Companies Registration and Commercial Registration sections jointly
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full incorporation package (notarized constitutional documents, capital deposit certificate, shareholder information) to the GAFI OSS registrar. The registrar checks compliance, collects the statutory incorporation fee (USD 650 equivalent in EGP) and issues the commercial registration certificate (Commercial Registry extract), tax card certificate, and pension fund registration notification.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Capital deposit certificate from the bank
Name reservation certificate
Form of incorporation (GAFI Form 1A)
Directors' and shareholders' personal information statement
Proof of registered address / tenancy agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues an inquiry notice, respond within 30 days with supplementary evidence such as corrected document pages or clarification letter signed by legal counsel. If the requested corrections are invalid, file a formal objection through the GAFI Complaints and Appeals Unit, which must issue a decision within 60 days under statutory policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Authority for Social Insurance (NASSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, automatically assigned tax registration number (Tax Card) is generated via GAFI-ETA integration. The company must voluntarily register for value-added tax (VAT) if taxable supplies exceed EGP threshold applicable to digital services. Simultaneously confirm 30 days from commercial registration to enroll the managing director and all employees with NASSI. Corporate income tax registration for all shareholders is mandatory.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Tax Card application / VAT registration form
Lease contract of the registered office
List of shareholders and their national IDs
Copy of Memorandum summarizing activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA challenges the VAT registration effective date or classification, provide a written interpretation using the applicable VAT executive regulations with legal counsel opinion. For pension disputes, NASSI may issue arrears calculation; appeal through the internal administrative body prior to any court action.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) – Digital Services Regulation Office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration of Remote Digital Services and Software License (Voluntary Certification) – no physical operating permit required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based software development and data processing activity with no physical manufacturing or hazardous pollutants
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to fully digital SaaS operations; incidental building-level waste must meet local municipal solid waste regulations and if a physical server room is installed, EEAA indoor air and thermal regulations require HVAC standards consistency with Egyptian Electricity Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For commercial office lease exceeding 500 m² or employing more than 50 persons, Civil Defense Department fire safety certificate is mandatory. The office space must pass structural and occupancy load verification by the district municipality engineering office, and an occupational safety and health clearance is required if using dedicated server infrastructure or battery storage rooms.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; official portal https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoicing clearance portal https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must: (1) incorporate and obtain an Arabic-notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation and board resolution; (2) register for a tax card (statutory TIN) with the ETA via the unified TAX platform or the competent tax office, submitting the entity contract, legal representative POA, Egyptian registered address, and bank account evidence; (3) mandatorily register for VAT under Law No. 67 of 2016 if annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000, or voluntarily register to claim input VAT and export refunds; (4) onboard to the ETA e-invoicing system and obtain the unique ETA registration certificate and QR/API credentials; non-resident LLCs without a fixed establishment but deriving Egyptian-source income must also register for tax and file under the withholding regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person subject to corporate income tax at the statutory rate of 22.5% on worldwide net taxable income, with no pass-through to shareholders; distributions to foreign shareholders may trigger additional withholding tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; LLC income is mandatorily taxed at entity level. Available statutory mechanisms: (1) voluntary VAT registration for exporters below the EGP 500,000 threshold; (2) VAT group treatment for closely related exporting entities; (3) consolidated income tax filing for Egyptian groups with ownership of at least 90%; (4) small-taxpayer simplified regime for annual turnover below EGP 10,000,000; (5) foreign tax credit elections and treaty treaty-based relief applications; Egypt has not enacted OECD hybrid mismatch legislation, so no domestic hybrid-mismatch election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies for mandatory VAT registration; voluntary registration is permitted for exporters and zero-rated suppliers; the e-invoicing mandate applies to all VAT-registered taxpayers
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The ETA operates a real-time fiscal clearance e-invoicing and e-receipt regime; every business-to-business invoice and relevant receipt must be transmitted in JSON/XML to the ETA clearance platform before issuance, validated digitally, and stamped with a QR code and unique UUID; integration must use the ETA REST APIs from certified ERP/accounting systems; export zero-rated invoices must include the export indicator and supporting evidence codes, and invoices not cleared by the ETA are fiscally invalid and may be disallowed for input credit and refund purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 16 of the Egyptian VAT Law applies to: (1) goods physically exported outside Egypt and supported by official customs export documentation; (2) services, including MarTech SaaS and SEO analytics subscriptions, supplied to a non-resident recipient and wholly consumed outside Egypt, provided the place of supply is treated as outside Egypt and the consideration is received in foreign currency through a licensed Egyptian bank; (3) international transport services and ancillary services; the exporter must maintain a complete evidentiary file and clear the invoice through the ETA e-invoicing platform.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ETA-cleared export e-invoice with export code, QR validation, and full detail of the SaaS/SEO analytics service scope
Signed commercial contract or subscription agreement with the non-resident customer evidencing offshore place of supply and foreign-currency consideration
Customs export declaration with matching export invoice (required when any hardware, data pipelines, or physical media are bundled with the software service)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export of any bundled goods
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Egyptian bank evidencing actual receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Central Bank of Egypt export proceeds confirmation/repatriation statement and annual reconciliation listing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audit teams scrutinize zero-rating claims through invoice-level reconciliation, bank FX certificates, and customs records; fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating triggers reassessment of VAT at the standard 14% rate on the gross consideration, a monthly delay penalty of 2% on unpaid VAT until full settlement, administrative fines up to EGP 500,000, retrospective clawback of refunded amounts with a 100% surcharge, suspension of refund rights for up to five years, and imprisonment penalties of up to five years for tax evasion under Article 86 of Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), Banking Law No. 194 of 2020 as amended, and the Foreign Exchange Control regulations issued by the CBE
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a managed float regime for the EGP. Current account transactions are generally freely convertible and supported by banks, but capital account transactions require CBE approval or registration. Profit and dividend remittances are permissible after corporate tax settlement and audited financial statements, but may encounter administrative delays and prioritization of essential imports during periods of FX scarcity. In practice, full convertibility for services/SaaS revenue is subject to CBE circulars and bank-specific compliance filters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated into Egypt within the statutory period (generally up to 90 days from the date of shipment or notification, with limited extensions by the CBE). Proceeds are required to be sold or converted into EGP in the local banking market in full unless a specific exemption or non-surrender allowance is granted under CBE Circular No. 38 of 2023 and related instructions, which impose mandatory surrender ratios of up to 100% for most exported services, including technology and SEO content analytics tools.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMI-only banking. Offshore electronic money institutions and virtual IBAN providers are not licensed or supervised by the CBE. They cannot maintain settlement accounts in Egypt or provide commercial banking services to an Egyptian LLC without obtaining a CBE branch or e-payment license. Foreign EMIs may only serve as informational invoicing tools, but all actual EGP and FX settlement must occur through CBE-licensed banks. Use of non-compliant offshore EMI rails creates AML and exchange-control violation risks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial corporate account opening. The legal representative, general manager, or at least one authorized signatory with legal capacity must appear in person before the bank's compliance officer. Remote opening is not permitted for foreign-owned Egyptian LLCs. Non-resident shareholders who are not signatories may appoint a resident or a nominated director by notarized and legalized power of attorney, but the appointed individual must attend the KYC interview physically in Egypt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract showing full shareholding ladder, notarized UBO declaration, passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners, and proof of source of wealth for all non-resident shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore SaaS revenue concentration and digital service export profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited SaaS revenue trail, Stripe/Paddle payout statements with clear subscription metadata, client contracts, export invoice register, and service delivery evidence sufficient to differentiate from potential money laundering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection through cross-border wire from non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution stating capital contribution purpose, bank reference letters from the originating banks, source-of-funds evidence, and demonstration of underlying software IP ownership or licensing agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low-risk tech entity with high transaction velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML compliance policy, transaction volume forecast, Google Analytics user metrics, and enterprise client list with country-level billing segmentation to support legitimate cross-border recurring revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment rails named as Stripe and Paddle while using Egyptian bank accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clear reconciliation mapping of FX conversion and net settlement entries, payment service provider verification letters, and a commitment to maintain separate EGP operational account provisional ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for an Egyptian LLC must be routed through a CBE-licensed bank in the name of the Egyptian company. The bank will require a board resolution, shareholder invoice or contribution statement, a purpose code aligned with CBE's Balance of Payments manual for foreign direct investment (FDI), and proof of corporate existence. The receiving bank will map the wire to capital suspense, then convert or register the contribution in EGP following CBE rules. SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank is the standard channel. Verification includes KYC/QI checks and registration with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) or banks must register the inward remittance via CBE's Electronic Reporting System.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements and international software-related vendor payments are executed through CBE-licensed banks using SWIFT MT103 for open-account foreign currency payments. For high-value or high-risk transactions, commercial letters of credit (MT700) may be required, especially where goods or services involve Egyptian import and tax documentation. Outbound payments require underlying contracts, commercial invoices, tax registration (tax card), taxpayer identification, and evidence of withholding tax compliance. All FX outflows must comply with the CBE's purpose codes for service imports and are subject to interbank rate and availability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forwards on major trade currencies based on underlying exposure, transacted only through CBE-licensed banks and subject to genuine trade documentation.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing EGP for those exposures where contractual settlement is in a freely convertible currency.
Plain vanilla cross-currency swaps for EGP/USD and primary payment currency pairs, limited to hedging underlying commercial obligations.
Foreign currency options in limited cases, only with CBE-approved local banks and minimum hedge tenors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 11) for the Egyptian LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year LLCs, on or before 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers fixed late-filing penalties plus a monthly late-payment surcharge on the due tax under the Egyptian Tax Procedures Law. Continued non-compliance enables ETA to issue assessment notices, attach bank accounts, and request GAFI to restrict the company's commercial registry activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement and notes) submitted to the companies registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year; for calendar-year LLCs, on or before 30 June, after approval by the shareholders' general assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GAFI may issue non-compliance notices, impose administrative late fees, suspend the company's electronic registration privileges, and after repeated defaults initiate involuntary administrative strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial register status verification and update of members, managers and beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Commercial Registry via the electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the company's commercial registration; any in-year share transfer or manager change must be filed within 15 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to keep commercial registry and real-beneficiary records current exposes managers to fines under the Commercial Registry Law and the AML Law. Incorrect status retained after official reminders may lead to GAFI administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recurring monthly VAT and payroll/withholding tax declarations (aggregated as the annual standing tax calendar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly, no later than 30 days after the end of the VAT month for VAT; payroll/withholding returns follow the ETA schedule for the applicable fiscal month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each late or missing monthly return attracts a statutory late-filing penalty and a monthly late-payment surcharge. Persistent non-filing after official notices exposes the LLC to enforced collection and, in aggravated cases, a criminal tax-evasion referral.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC must appoint a licensed external auditor and produce audited financial statements when any of the following conditions exists: the LLC exceeds the GAFI/Companies Law size thresholds; the LLC has more than 50 members; the shareholders or lenders require an audit; or the LLC's annual gross turnover exceeds EGP 2,000,000 for Egyptian Tax Authority certification purposes. A dormant LLC may request a formal audit waiver from GAFI and ETA only where no transactions occurred during the financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Financial Reporting Standards (EFRS), which are aligned with IFRS; statutory financial statements filed with GAFI must be prepared in Arabic with the Egyptian pound as the reporting currency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt does not levy a separate annual UBO return for a standard closed LLC. The manager(s) must maintain the Register of Real Beneficiaries continuously and file a GAFI registry update within 15 days of any share transfer or beneficial ownership change. At the annual general meeting approving the financial statements, members re-confirm the share register and any transfers recorded during the year. If GAFI issues an electronic data call, the LLC must respond within the specified deadline.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 750 per year for a GAFI-registered office or local compliance agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 per year for a MarTech/Analytics SaaS LLC, subject to transaction volume and dormant-company reductions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% headline corporate income tax (CIT) rate for resident LLCs under Law No. 91 of 2005; non-resident branch profits additionally attract a 10% branch remittance tax on repatriated after-tax profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard resident LLCs enjoy no statutory tax holiday; however, Law No. 152 of 2022 introduces a simplified turnover-based tax of 0.5%-2.5% for small businesses with annual revenues up to EGP 20 million; free-zone established entities may benefit from a 0% CIT rate on export-oriented activities; immediate expensing and accelerated depreciation for certain digital assets and software R&D are available in limited circumstances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 21 for legal persons; mandatory electronic filing through the Egypt Tax Authority (ETA) portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg with authenticated tax ID and encrypted submission.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance CIT installments are payable during the fiscal year (e.g., quarterly in months 4, 6, 10 and 12 for calendar-year taxpayers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form No. 21 must be filed within four months after the end of the tax year (Article 87, Law No. 91 of 2005); for a calendar-year LLC, the deadline is April 30 of the following year; any tax payable is due simultaneously with the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the LLC, commercial registration number, tax card number and Egyptian Tax ID (for the SEO Content Analytics Tool entity).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not listed in the return; the LLC itself must quote the valid Egyptian tax card and register all foreign parent, intermediary and beneficial owner details separately with the ETA beneficial ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis (cash/accrual), financial statement currency and fiscal year; reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income is disclosed here.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Egyptian GAAP or IFRS as adopted in Egypt must be used; non-resident owners must ensure the EGP conversion is performed at the Central Bank of Egypt exchange rate for all USD-denominated Stripe/Paddle receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all sources: SaaS subscriptions, keyword analytics licenses, SEO data crawler usage fees, and API-based content analytics revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue is Egyptian-sourced where services are effectively used by Egyptian customers or where the crawler infrastructure is located in Egypt; a PE-dependent sourcing schedule must support non-resident allocation claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs: employee compensation, cloud hosting, data center leasing, software maintenance, marketing, legal and professional fees, and amortization of capitalized crawler/software development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign head-office or parent-company charges (royalties, management fees, IP license fees) are deductible only if the LLC proves actual service delivery, economic benefit, and arm's-length pricing via contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from previous years and offset against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses realized by the Egyptian tax resident entity are eligible; losses of non-resident shareholders or foreign group entities cannot be used against Egyptian LLC income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: disallowed expenses, thin capitalization interest disallowance, transfer pricing adjustments, and any treaty-based exemption claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to the foreign parent for analytics software IP must comply with Egyptian transfer pricing rules and the arm's-length standard; failure to attach the TP disclosure will automatically trigger review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of CIT at 22.5%, subtraction of quarterly advance payments, foreign tax credits if applicable, and final payment or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders claiming treaty credits must provide ETA-certified documentation; no dividend WHT credit is available to the LLC unless the dividend withholding was legally imposed and paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure form identifying all related-party transactions, amounts, jurisdictions, selected methods, and comparables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian LLC must attach Attachment B and be ready to submit Master File, Local File, and country-by-country reporting notifications when the statutory EGP 8,000,000 related-party turnover threshold is exceeded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EGP 500 for each month or fraction of a month of delay, in addition to late-payment surcharge of 2% per month on unpaid tax from the statutory due date; under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 202 of 2023, willful failure can trigger fines of EGP 20,000-50,000, attachment of bank accounts, and criminal prosecution for responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax on distributions by Egyptian resident LLCs to shareholders (Article 52, Law No. 91 of 2005); the rate applies on the gross dividend and is retained and remitted by the LLC to the ETA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (1) Shareholder obtains a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence; (2) the LLC submits a treaty relief application, TRC, beneficial ownership declaration and shareholding structure to the ETA Large Taxpayer Office prior to distribution; (3) ETA may issue an advance reduced-withholding authorization (typically processed within 30-60 days); (4) if domestic 10% rate was already withheld, the non-resident shareholder may file a refund claim under the applicable DTA; reduced rates generally require a 10% or 25% ownership threshold depending on the treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding: 20% on royalties paid to non-residents and 20% on interest paid to non-residents; applicable DTA treaties commonly reduce royalty WHT to 10-15% and interest WHT to 5-10%, subject to beneficial ownership, substance, and arm's-length pricing validation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8,000,000 aggregate annual related-party transaction value; exceeding this ETA threshold mandates the preparation and submission of a comprehensive Transfer Pricing Disclosure with the annual CIT return, plus full Local File and Master File documentation prepared contemporaneously; Country-by-Country reporting applies at consolidated group revenue thresholds under Egyptian decrees.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, Law No. 91 of 2005 Article 103 (general anti-abuse rule), the Unified Tax Procedures Law, and the beneficial ownership register requirements impose a comprehensive substance-over-form standard: the LLC must demonstrate active management, real employees, local decision-making, and genuine commercial activity to secure treaty benefits, avoid PE creation, and prevent recharacterization of intercompany arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion and False Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understatement of Stripe/Paddle subscription receipts, unrecorded cash-equivalent crypto payments, hidden offshore bank accounts, or fabrication of deductible expenses to suppress taxable profit below the 22.5% CIT charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine equal to at least the amount of tax evaded plus imprisonment under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended; civil recovery of evaded tax, late-payment surcharge of 2% per month, and a further 10% administrative penalty on the understated tax; ETA may seize bank accounts and freeze payment gateways.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, shadow directors, and beneficial owners who signed false returns or directed evasion are personally and jointly liable for evaded tax; courts may impose asset attachment, travel bans, aviation and land exit bans, and prison sentences of up to several years, and the corporate veil will be pierced where funds were diverted to owners without legal distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Substance Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating EG_LLC as an invoicing shell: no employees in Egypt, no physical office, all key decisions taken abroad, no bank account substance, and the parent retains the entire commercial risk for the SEO analytics software IP while the Egyptian entity merely books commissions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA recharacterization of the entity as a fiscal fiction; full 22.5% CIT imposed on deemed Egyptian-source profit, denial of all notional management fee deductions, disallowance of treaty advantages, and application of Article 103 GAAR with additional 20% adjustment penalty and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The sole nominee director and non-resident beneficial owner face piercing of the corporate veil where no formal shareholder resolution or arm's-length compensation was recorded; personal civil exposure for the full tax, interest and penalties; criminal liability for knowingly structuring a sham company to escape Egyptian tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border related-party payments (e.g., analytics software royalties, cloud licensing fees, or management charges to the foreign parent) exceeding the EGP 8,000,000 threshold without contemporaneous Local File, Master File, or Attachment B transfer pricing disclosure; booking a zero or artificially low profit margin while foreign affiliates retain upside.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA TP audit requiring an upward adjustment to the Egyptian entity's taxable income, a 20% accuracy-related penalty on the understated tax, late-payment interest of 2% per month, and potential re-qualification of royalty payments as hidden profit distributions subject to 10% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: CFO and directors who approved defective TP documentation may be held liable for the additional tax and penalties under the responsible-officer doctrine; in flagrant cases of deliberate transfer of profits, imprisonment and travel restrictions apply alongside personal restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the real ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of EG_LLC in the Egyptian electronic register, concealment of the foreign parent's ownership chain through bearer-like share arrangements, or processing Stripe/Paddle payouts through opaque intermediaries to disguise the economic beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended) ranging from EGP 50,000 to EGP 500,000 for UBO registration violations; criminal sanctions of up to seven years' imprisonment for participating in concealment, money laundering or financing arrangements, plus confiscation of the LLC's assets and closure of local bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the compliance officer bear personal criminal liability for failure to file UBO disclosures; travel bans and asset freezes are routinely imposed during investigation; piercing of the corporate veil permits recovery of laundered funds from directors' personal estates where corporate records are adjudged artificially manipulated.
